Wikipedia: Simone Martini, Duccio's pupil, is among the Sienese school's most important artists

highlight.text: Perpetuating the Sienese tradition, Simone's style contrasted with the sobriety and monumentality of Florentine art, and is noted for its soft, stylized, decorative features, sinuosity of line, and courtly elegance.

work.text: Simone's most consummate works are his frescoes at Assisi, the central portion of the Annunciation of the Uffizi, and his St Louis of Toulouse crowning Robert of Anjou.
Saint Louis of Toulouse Crowning His Brother Robert of Anjou is a painting by Simone Martini, commissioned from him by Robert of Anjou during the artist's stay in Naples around 1317.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Saint Louis of Toulouse Crowning His Brother Robert of Anjou

work.text: St. Louis, Archbishop of Toulouse, of life size, sits in majesty with the mitre on his head and a crozier in his right hand ; and with his left holds a crown over the head of his kneeling brother, Robert of Naples. Two diminutive angels flying above St. Louis hold over his head the crown of sanctity.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

moment.text: There is no reason to doubt that about 1315 Simone was an artist of considerable powers, known by repute not only at Siena, but throughout the continent of Italy.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

moment.text: Simone's art owes much to French manuscript illumination and ivory carving: examples of such art were brought to Siena in the fourteenth century by means of the Via Francigena, a main pilgrimage and trade route from Northern Europe to Rome.

matters.text: It shows Robert being crowned by his elder brother Louis of Toulouse, who was made a saint in 1317.

matters.text: [Louis] had solemnly renounced his rights to the crown of Naples in Robert's favour, “preferring a heavenly crown to an earthly.” Robert of Anjou determined to celebrate his brother's canonisation with great pomp and with acts of princely generosity.
